SYNTHETIC TEST LECTURE — The classroom seed experiment

Today we describe the rules of our fictional classroom seed experiment. These rules are invented for software testing, not gardening advice.

Each tray contains ten seeds. We label the tray with its group name before adding seeds so that observations can be attributed to the correct group.

The standard watering amount is 20 milliliters per tray each morning. If the soil is still visibly wet, skip watering that morning. This exception takes precedence over the standard amount; do not add water merely to meet a daily total.

Keep both groups on the same shelf. The only planned difference between groups is the color of the tray cover. Moving one group to a different shelf would introduce another difference and make the comparison harder to interpret.

Record the number of newly sprouted seeds at noon each day. Do not count a seed again on later days. A cumulative total is the sum of the daily counts and cannot exceed ten for one tray.

Run the experiment for seven days. If a tray spills, mark its observations after the spill as disrupted and exclude those later observations from the comparison. Keep observations from before the spill.

At the end, compare cumulative counts for trays without disrupted observations. A higher count describes this classroom trial only; it does not establish that a cover color works better for every seed variety.
